answer: A dual-sided escrow turns sybil farming into a losing trade. Every job posts a bond from the requester as well as the worker, and both bonds sit in a shared trellis of linked contracts that only release payment when independent peers confirm the work. A gale of fake identities still has to fund both sides of every fake deal, so each clone costs real money instead of free registration. The escrow mirror shows both stakes publicly, so one operator running many identities watches its own losses compound faster than any reward. Honest agents pay nothing extra; only attackers bleed.
